summary: Extends the IMAP PARTIAL SEARCH return option so clients can page through search results or limit how many come back. It also clarifies interactions with other IMAP extensions. It updates RFCs 4731 and 5267.

eli5.summary: When you search a huge mailbox, you can ask for the first ten answers, then the next ten, instead of all at once.

questions: how to page through imap search results
what does partial nil mean in imap
subtitle: How IMAP clients can ask for a slice of a big search or fetch result instead of everything at once.

tldr.problem: A search in a huge mailbox can match tens of thousands of messages, and returning them all wastes server work, network and client memory.
tldr.mechanism: The PARTIAL extension adds a PARTIAL return option to SEARCH and a PARTIAL modifier to UID FETCH. Each takes a range such as 1:500 (from the oldest match) or -1:-100 (from the newest) and returns only that slice.
tldr.outcome: Clients can page through results, and servers can optimise their work. It is a Proposed Standard that updates RFC 4731 and RFC 5267 and clarifies how they interact with RFC 9051.

today: RFC 9394 is a Proposed Standard published in June 2023. It is not obsoleted and has no later updates listed. It updates RFC 4731 and RFC 5267.

sections.title: Introduction and Overview
sections.content:
RFC 9394 defines the PARTIAL extension to the Internet Message Access Protocol (IMAP). It lets a client limit how many SEARCH results come back and perform incremental, paged searches. The RFC says this also helps servers optimise resource usage.

The extension works with both IMAP4rev1 (RFC 3501) and IMAP4rev2 (RFC 9051) and uses the extensibility rules of RFC 4466. It extends the PARTIAL SEARCH return option first specified in RFC 5267, and it clarifies some interactions between RFC 5267 and RFCs 4731 and 9051.

A server advertises support by including the PARTIAL capability in its CAPABILITY response or response code. The acknowledgments say the document was motivated by a team at Yahoo! and their questions about best client practices for large mailboxes.
sections.eli5: Email programs often have to deal with mailboxes with a huge number of letters. This document gives them a polite way to ask for just a few at a time.

sections.title: Paged SEARCH Results
sections.content:
The PARTIAL SEARCH return option makes the server put a subset of the results into an ESEARCH response. The subset is given by a mandatory range. The first result, the message with the lowest matching UID, is number 1. So PARTIAL 1:500 asks for the first 500 results and PARTIAL 501:1000 for the second 500. This intentionally mirrors message sequence numbers.

A client can also count from the newest match by putting a minus sign in front of the numbers. -1 is the last message, -2 the next to last, and so on. The RFC notes that this syntax helps server implementations optimise their SEARCHes.

A single command MUST NOT contain more than one PARTIAL or ALL return option: either one PARTIAL, one ALL, or neither. The full list of results MUST be ordered in mailbox order, meaning UID or message sequence number order.

If a range reaches past the end of the results, the server returns the results that exist. The reply echoes the original range, and the set of results may be shorter than the range. If the whole range lies beyond the results, the server returns the special value NIL instead of a sequence set. Clients need not request pages in any particular order.

Because a mailbox can change while a client pages through it, the RFC suggests using PARTIAL together with UPDATE from RFC 5267 when the server also advertises CONTEXT=SEARCH. The two options do not interact: UPDATE gives notifications for all matching results.
sections.eli5: You can ask for results by position, like "the first 500" or "the 100 newest." If you ask for a page that is past the end of the pile, you just get "nothing there."

sections.title: Combining PARTIAL with MIN, MAX, COUNT and SAVE
sections.content:
This section applies when the server advertises PARTIAL or CONTEXT=SEARCH, together with ESEARCH and/or IMAP4rev2. The SAVE result option does not change whether the server returns items for PARTIAL. As in Section 3.1, asking for both PARTIAL and ALL in one SEARCH command is an error.

What the saved $ marker refers to depends on the options combined with SAVE:

  • SAVE PARTIAL: the messages returned by PARTIAL.
  • SAVE PARTIAL MIN or MAX: the PARTIAL messages plus the MIN or MAX message.
  • SAVE PARTIAL MIN MAX: the PARTIAL messages plus the MIN and MAX messages.
  • SAVE PARTIAL COUNT (optionally with MIN and/or MAX): all messages found by the search, because the server returns both PARTIAL and COUNT.
sections.eli5: If you also ask the server to remember your answer, the rules say exactly what it remembers. Usually it is just the page you asked for, but if you also ask for a count, it remembers everything it found.

sections.title: PARTIAL for UID FETCH
sections.content:
The extension also adds a PARTIAL FETCH modifier to the UID FETCH command. It has the same syntax as the SEARCH return option. When present, the server returns FETCH results only for messages in the given range of the requested set. This is useful when the sequence-set in the first parameter of UID FETCH covers an unknown number of messages.

In the RFC's example, UID FETCH 25900:26600 (UID FLAGS) (PARTIAL -1:-3) returns data for the last 3 messages in that UID range, and the same command with PARTIAL 1:5 returns the first 5.

Section 3.4 is informative. The PARTIAL modifier can be combined with the CHANGEDSINCE modifier from RFC 7162 (CONDSTORE). The server first selects the requested slice, such as the last 30 messages, and then returns only those whose modification sequence is higher than the given value. The order of the two modifiers does not matter.
sections.eli5: The same "just a page, please" trick works when you ask the server for details about many messages. You can even say "of the newest 30, show me only the ones that changed."

sections.title: Formal Syntax
sections.content:
The syntax is given in ABNF. A partial-range is either partial-range-first (two positive numbers such as 1:500, searching from oldest to newest) or partial-range-last (two numbers each preceded by a minus sign such as -500:-400, searching from newest to oldest). A range written the other way round, like 500:400, means the same as 400:500. Unlike a normal sequence range it cannot contain the asterisk wildcard.

The server's answer is PARTIAL (range results), where the results are either a sequence set or NIL, meaning no results correspond to the requested range. The same modifier-partial is used as a SEARCH return option and as a FETCH modifier. All alphabetic tokens are case insensitive, and implementations MUST accept them that way.
sections.eli5: This part is the exact spelling guide, so every email program writes and reads "the first ten" the same way.

sections.title: Security and IANA Considerations
sections.content:
The extension adds one IMAP capability and does not change the underlying security considerations of IMAP4rev1 and IMAP4rev2. The authors and reviewers believe no new security issues are introduced.

The RFC describes it as an optimisation that can reduce both the work done by the server and the data returned to the client, and likely lowers memory use on both sides. It warns, however, that this is new code in both client and server, so rigorous testing is required to avoid new implementation bugs. IANA has added PARTIAL to the IMAP Capabilities registry with RFC 9394 as the reference.
sections.eli5: Asking for smaller pages does not open any new doors for bad guys. The only risk is that programmers make mistakes in new code, so they need to test it well.

data.title: Asking for the first 500 results
data.code:
C: A03 UID SEARCH RETURN (PARTIAL 1:500) UNDELETED
    UNKEYWORD $Junk
S: * ESEARCH (TAG "A03") UID PARTIAL (1:500 ...)
// 500 results in set syntax elided.
S: A03 OK Completed.

C: A04 UID SEARCH RETURN (PARTIAL 24000:24500) UNDELETED
    UNKEYWORD $Junk
S: * ESEARCH (TAG "A04") UID PARTIAL (24000:24500 NIL)
// No results are present; this is beyond the end of the results.
S: A04 OK Completed.
